claim.quote: The combination of this result with searches by the CMS experiment for H $\to\mathrm{b\overline{b}}$ in other production processes yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations and a signal strength of 1.04 $\pm$ 0.20.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 121, 121801 (2018)

name: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

significance.quote: an observed (expected) significance of 5.6 (5.5) standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS saw the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks, which is what it does most of the time but is very hard to pick out from the flood of ordinary collisions.
summary.technical: VH production with 41.3 fb^-1 of 2017 data gives 4.8 sigma at m_H = 125.09 GeV; combined with 7, 8 and 13 TeV VH data and with other production modes the observed (expected) significance is 5.6 (5.5) sigma, signal strength 1.04 +/- 0.20.

title: Observation of Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks
why_it_matters: H -> bb is the dominant Higgs decay; observing it at the predicted rate confirmed the standard model picture of how the Higgs boson decays.
